body: Company store models (e.g. '$0.4M investment, ~1-year payback') are targets with undefined numerators. They are often net of tenant allowances and payables, and they exclude network capex (DCs, systems). Divide the 10-K/MD&A capex budgeted for new stores by planned gross openings, then rebuild: build-out − tenant allowance + inventory net of payables + pre-opening (from the pre-opening note). If reconciling needs a tenant allowance above ~40% of build-out, treat the headline as stale or narrowly defined and recompute the payback. Add DC capex ÷ stores served. Five Below FY26: $100M / ~155 openings ≈ $0.65M gross vs '$0.4M'; implied payback ~1.6-1.9 years, not ~1. Also diff the store-model paragraph year over year: unchanged numbers through cost inflation are a flag.
title: Triangulate a retailer's headline 'new store investment/payback' against its own capex-per-new-store guidance
